key_insight: Global relaxed entropy-energy states can be constructed for dynamic thermoplasticity even when the temperature-dependent yield set collapses, but macroscopic Prandtl–Reuss normality is not guaranteed.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies what thermoplastic models can predict when heating eliminates shear resistance, without viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load assumption.
method: Use a one-parameter Temam–Norton–Hoff–Galerkin approximation with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heating.
Establish logarithmic-temperature compactness and stress admissibility through entropy-weighted estimates.
Represent limiting plastic behavior with support-weighted measures and fibre lifts preserving exact normality.
evidence_signal: Analytical results include an overstress convergence rate of O(√(log n/n)) in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and an explicit smooth counterexample to macroscopic normality; the abstract reports no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Available compactness does not identify a canonical macroscopic stress–plastic-flow pairing; complete yield collapse can also permit non-measure plastic flow or loss of the full displacement boundary trace.
paper_title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
